messages:
rhea: quick check: for the new inference-config endpoint do we: 1) keep backend gRPC+proto and have gateway transcode to JSON, or 2) flatten to REST everywhere?

tom: strong vote for gRPC backend. typed contracts catch a lot of integration bugs.

noor: +1, but we need a documented header canonicalization. x-tenant vs tenant-id ambiguity caused support tickets.

chris: operationally, quotas are tricky. gateway can enforce tenant quotas (good for external traffic), backend should only audit. need explicit ownership field in route config.

rhea: sketch of route config idea:

  - path: /v1/infer
    to: inference-config.svc:grpc
    transcode: true
    propagate: [x-tenant, x-request-id, x-replay-safe]
    quota_owner: gateway

noor: telemetry: gRPC trailers carry kv-cache-hit counts. gateway must copy them into response headers or we lose signals. propose trailer->x-trailer-* mapping.

tom: error mapping table proposal: include original gRPC code and message in JSON body as fields (grpc_code, grpc_message) and map to HTTP status for routing.

chris: sidecar vs shared gateway: sidecar keeps traces local and reduces cross-gateway fanout, but multiplies images and complicates rollout. hybrid approach ok: shared gateway + opt-in sidecar for latency-critical routes.

infra-bot: canary scheduled: gateway-transcode-e2e v0.3 -> canary 2025-09-30T22:00Z

rhea: action items: noor doc header canonicalization + tests; tom draft error-mapping json spec; chris define quota migration playbook; i'll open RFC and link deploy plan.

noor: I'll add unit tests that assert trailer copying and header names.

chris: I'll draft migration checklist for services switching quota_owner to gateway.

tom: +1 on RFC. small nit: add a console toggle to show either REST contract or generated proto SDKs for any route.

rhea: agreed. if no objections i'll open the RFC PR later today. :thumbsup:
